problem_analysis: The core challenge is the joint optimization of INA placement and worker-to-aggregator assignment under strict constraints: a finite INA switch budget, per-switch processing capacity, and per-link bandwidth limits. The solution must balance load distribution across the network while respecting topology-aware routing and the critical 'last-hop' bottleneck at the PS. The key insight is that placement and assignment are interdependent, requiring a coordinated strategy that avoids hotspots and underutilization.
strategy_overview: The solution follows a constructive, top-down pipeline: first, it constructs a prioritized candidate set for INA placement based on network topology and job demand; second, it assigns workers to aggregation points using a greedy, capacity-aware assignment that respects placement decisions; finally, it assembles the final solution by combining placement and routing decisions, leveraging existing infrastructure for makespan evaluation.

function_architecture.name: _build_placement_candidates
function_architecture.strategic_role: Identifies and ranks a subset of candidate switches for INA deployment based on their strategic position in the network topology and their potential to alleviate congestion, considering job distribution and pod-level bandwidth constraints.

outputs.name: placement_candidates
outputs.description: A filtered and ordered list of switch Node IDs eligible for INA, prioritized by topological influence.

function_architecture.name: _assign_workers_to_aggregators
function_architecture.strategic_role: Assigns each worker to a single aggregation point—either an INA-enabled switch or the PS—while respecting the INA placement decision, capacity limits, and routing constraints, ensuring no worker is assigned to an unselected switch.

outputs.description: Mapping from job index and worker index to the Node ID of the assigned aggregation point.

function_architecture.strategic_role: Orchestrates the entire heuristic pipeline by executing the placement and assignment steps in sequence, validates the resulting configuration, and returns the final solution in the required schema.
